title: PO Regulations 2024 — Foundation, Structure & Key Definitions
official_text:
📜 THE POST OFFICE REGULATIONS, 2024

Notified vide Notification No. S.O. 5440(E) dated 16th December, 2024

Attribute Detail
Parent ActPost Office Act, 2023 (Act No. 43 of 2023)
Power underSection 13 of the Post Office Act, 2023
Notification Date16th December, 2024
Commencement16th day of December, 2024
Structure15 Chapters, 180 Regulations, 5 Schedules

Regulation 2 — Key Definitions

Term Definition (Verbatim)
Accountable Items Items that provide a receipt at the time of booking for track and trace (stage wise electronic data on movement of item) and require the signature (in ink or digital) of the addressee, the payee, or their authorised person upon receipt of an item, to provide evidence of delivery. Includes: India Post Parcel, Speed Post, Magazine Post, International Speed Post Services (EMS), International Air Parcels, International Tracked Packets, International Registered Letter items, Money Order and items with value added services like registration, insurance and cash on delivery (COD).
Addressee The intended recipient or the person to whom any item is to be delivered.
Authorised Person A person, duly authorised by the addressee to receive the item or by a payee to receive the money on his behalf.
Delivery The delivery of an item at the address of the addressee, or to the addressee or other person or location considered to be authorised to receive the item according to the usual manner of delivering items to the addressee.
In Course of Transmission by Post The period starting from receipt of an item by the post office to its delivery to the addressee or return to the sender or otherwise disposed of.
Letter Box A box installed in post offices or mail offices or at public places, for posting of fully prepaid letters, postcards, letter cards and book post items.
Payee The person who intends to receive money through money remittance services.
Post Any system for collection, clearance, sorting, dispatch, conveyance, and delivery of items by the postal network.
Postmaster The Director or Chief Postmaster of general post office, or Senior Postmaster or Head Postmaster of head post office, or an officer exercising the powers of Postmaster, as the case may be, who is the head of such post office.
Redirection Action of assigning or directing an item to an address, other than the one to which it was initially addressed, for a specific reason.
Remitter The person who remits money through money remittance services.
Sender A person who sends any item.
Weight Gross weight or volumetric weight, whichever is higher, except when stated otherwise.
guru_explanation:
🧠 Guru's Take — Why This Matters

The PO Regulations 2024 is the operational bible for every postal employee. It was notified under Section 13 of the Post Office Act 2023 — the new Act that replaced the old Indian Post Office Act 1898. This regulation governs everything from how a letter is addressed to how compensation is paid. In the IP/PS exam, at least 4–6 questions come directly from these regulations every year.

🎯 The "Weight" Definition — A Classic Trap!

Weight means gross weight OR volumetric weight — whichever is HIGHER. This is a tricky MCQ trap. Many candidates assume it is always gross weight. Remember: if a large-volume but light item is sent, the volumetric weight may be higher, and that is what gets charged.

🔑 Three "Admin Instructions" Phrases to Remember

You will see the phrase "as specified by administrative instructions from time to time" throughout the regulations. This means that specific operational details (fees, forms, procedures) are NOT in the regulations themselves but in separate administrative orders issued by the Central Government or the Director General (as per Regs 178–180).

⚡ Exam Danger Zone

  • These regulations supersede previous rules where applicable. Do NOT cite older rules in answers.
  • Structure: 15 Chapters, 180 Regulations, 5 Schedules — likely to appear as a direct MCQ.
  • "Accountable items" include COD, insurance, and registered items — not just Speed Post.
  • "In course of transmission" starts from receipt by post office, not from posting in letter box.
practical_example:
📦 Practical Scenarios

Scenario 1 (Weight): A sender posts a large foam cushion weighing 300 grams, but its volumetric weight (calculated from dimensions) is 700 grams. Which weight is charged? → 700 grams (volumetric), as it is higher.

Scenario 2 (Accountable Item): A Speed Post item is posted in a letter box. Is this allowed? → No. Accountable items shall not be posted in letter boxes (Reg. 22). They must be presented at the post office counter.

Scenario 3 (In Course of Transmission): An item is lost after being collected from the sender's doorstep for Speed Post. Is the Post Office liable? → Yes, because "in course of transmission" begins from the moment of receipt by the post office (including doorstep pickup).
exam_insight:
📝 Top Exam Points — Regulations 1 & 2

  1. Notification No. = S.O. 5440(E) | Date = 16.12.2024
  2. Power source = Section 13, PO Act 2023
  3. Total structure = 15 Chapters + 180 Regulations + 5 Schedules
  4. "Weight" always means gross or volumetric — whichever is higher
  5. Accountable items = items with receipt + track & trace + signature on delivery
  6. "In course of transmission" starts from receipt by post office, ends at delivery/return/disposal
  7. Administrative instructions are issued under Regulations 178, 179 or 180

title: Business Hours, Postage & Postage Stamps — Complete Rules
official_text:
Regulation 3 — Business Hours

The business hours in a post office, during which business is transacted with the public, shall generally be as under on normal weekdays, which are not holidays for the Post Office or the Government:

Sl. No. Work Business Hours
(i)For references and enquiriesDuring the entire working hours of the office
(ii)Counter services including booking and posting of items, premium collection of insurance premiumsSix hours
(iii)Money remittance — Electronic Money Order, Indian Postal Order etc.Six hours
(iv)Savings BankSix hours

Reg. 3(2): Branch post offices shall be kept open for a maximum period of five hours in a day.

Regulations 5–7 — Postage Rules

  • Reg. 5(1): Postage shall generally be paid by modes mentioned in rule 9.
  • Reg. 5(2): The pre-payment of postage and other sums payable on an item shall be mandatory except otherwise mentioned in these regulations.
  • Reg. 6(2): Unpaid or insufficiently paid items are liable to be kept on hold for charging the postage due on them.

Regulation 7 — When Postage Is NOT Deemed Prepaid

Postage and other sums chargeable on an item shall not be deemed to be prepaid by means of a proper stamp or franking impression or point of sale receipt if —

  • (a) The stamp has not been provided for use as a postage stamp under these regulations;
  • (b) The stamp has been obliterated, defaced, torn, cut or otherwise rendered imperfect;
  • (c) The stamp has any word, letter, figure or design printed or impressed otherwise than by the Director General before posting; or
  • (d) The stamp has been cut, or otherwise, separated from an embossed envelope, or from a postcard or wrapper.

Proviso: Nothing in this regulation shall prevent the transmission of Book Now Pay Later (BNPL) items or other items as specified by administrative instructions from time to time.

Regulations 8–10 — Supply, Fraudulent Usage & Illegal Manufacture of Stamps

  • Reg. 8(2): No person or entity or institution or organisation or electronic platform shall sell or distribute postage stamps or deal in any other manner in postage stamps, except with the prior permission of the Director General.
  • Reg. 9(1): The act of usage of previously used postage stamp, fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to the Government, shall be punishable under the applicable law.
  • Reg. 9(2): If such postage stamp is detected on an item already posted, the item shall not be delivered.
  • Reg. 10(1): Illegal manufacturing and usage of forged, counterfeit, or fictitious postage stamps shall be punishable under the applicable law.

Regulation 13 — Types of Postage Stamps

Type of Stamp Description (Verbatim)
(a) Definitive Stamps Postage stamps, specifically issued to meet the day-to-day postage needs and are made available for sale for a period till stocks of a particular series last, which shall be printed and reprinted in different denominations as per the requirement of the post office.
(b) Commemorative Stamps Postage stamps issued to commemorate an event, institution, theme and personages, which shall be printed only once, in limited numbers and are sold for a limited period. They may be kept as collectible items and may be used for payment of postage.
(c) Special Stamps Postage stamps which are thematic like flora, fauna, architecture or art without commemorating any specific event.
(d) Joint Issue Stamps Postage stamps which are issued by India and any other country on mutually agreed terms and conditions.
(e) My Stamps Stamps which are issued on the basis of personalised or customised printing elements provided by the customer or proponent, subject to confirmation with administrative instructions.

Regulation 14 — Key Rules on Stamp Issuance

  • Reg. 14(5): No postage stamp shall be issued on a living personality.
  • Reg. 14(6): Stamp design and denomination shall be as approved by the Central Government.
  • Reg. 14(3): Proponents for a commemorative stamp relating to institutions or events must make a mandatory purchase of such stamps (Central Government may relax in exceptional cases).

Regulation 15 — Philatelic Advisory Committee

The Philatelic Advisory Committee shall advise on the issue of Commemorative Stamps, Special Stamps, and other allied matters. The Union Minister-in-Charge of the Ministry of Communications shall be the ex officio Chairperson.

Regulation 16 — Manner of Affixing Postage Stamps

  • Stamps affixed to an item must be completely adherent to the item itself and not to any part of its contents or any separate label.
  • The stamps should be affixed to the right-hand top corner of the address side.
  • The provisions of this regulation shall apply to franking of items in toto.
guru_explanation:
🧠 Guru's Memory Framework

Remember "6–6–6–5" for business hours: Counter, Money Remittance, Savings Bank = Six hours each; References = entire working hours; Branch Post Office = Five hours maximum.

💜 Stamp Types — The "D-C-S-J-M" Mnemonic

Use D-C-S-J-M: Definitive → Commemorative → Special → Joint Issue → My Stamps

  • Definitive = Daily use. Reprinted as needed.
  • Commemorative = One-time print, limited edition. Can be used for postage AND collected.
  • Special = Thematic (flora, fauna, art). No specific event being commemorated.
  • Joint Issue = India + another country, mutually agreed.
  • My Stamps = Customer's own personalised design.

⚡ High-Frequency Exam Points

  • No stamp on a living personality — this is absolute and unconditional.
  • Stamp design approved by Central Government, not Director General.
  • Philatelic Advisory Committee Chairperson = Union Minister of Communications (ex officio).
  • Stamps to be affixed at right-hand top corner of the address side.
  • Selling stamps without DG permission = punishable offence.
  • BNPL items are exempt from the "postage not prepaid" provision of Reg. 7.

title: Prohibition of Items, Delivery Rules & Undelivered Items
official_text:
Regulation 25 — Prohibition of Domestic Items

Subject to the provisions of these regulations, no person shall send by post —

Clause Prohibited Item
(a)Any explosive, dangerous, filthy, noxious or deleterious substance, any sharp instrument not properly protected, or any living creature which is either noxious or likely to injure items in course of transmission by post or any officer of the Post Office.
(b)Anything likely to injure, any item during transmission by post, or any officer of the Post Office.
(c)Any ticket, proposal, advertisement or any other matter relating to a lottery, except where the lottery is organised or authorised by the Central Government or State Government.
(d)Any indecent, immoral or obscene printing, painting, photograph, lithograph, engraving, book or card, or any other digital media, or any other indecent, immoral, or obscene item.
(i)Narcotics and psychotropic substances, as defined by the International Narcotics Control Board, or other illicit drugs.
(j)Counterfeit and pirated items.
(l)Dangerous goods, narcotics and psychotropic substances, prohibited drugs and cosmetics items, items prohibited by IATA, ICAO, Department of Wildlife and the Drug and Cosmetics Act, 1940 or items prohibited by any law of the land. Note: Battery and other items prohibited by air shall be sent through surface mode only.
(m)Live animals except otherwise permitted in these regulations.
(n)Coins, banknotes and other valuable items, except permitted through a special process. Currency notes, coins, or bank notes shall invariably be transmitted as insured items.

Regulations 41–43 — Delivery of Accountable Items

Regulation Key Rule
Reg. 41 — Accountable ItemsDelivery shall be made: (a) to the addressee or the authorized person — in case of registered item, insured item, Cash on Delivery, Money Order; (b) to the authorised person or on the address — in case of Speed Post item, India Post Parcel, etc.
Reg. 42 — Two Delivery AttemptsAn accountable item shall be issued for delivery and if not delivered on first presentation, it shall be issued once again for delivery. In case of inability to deliver after two attempts, it shall, in no case, be issued again for delivery. A notice of arrival shall be issued to the addressee.
Reg. 43 — Addressee to SignThe addressee of an accountable item or an authorised person shall sign in the receipt and proof of delivery, unless the outward appearance of the cover gives rise to suspicion of tampering. Where tampering is suspected, the item shall be opened at the post office in the presence of the Postmaster and contents entered in an inventory prepared in duplicate and signed by the addressee.

Regulation 52 — Delivery of Damaged Item

Where an accountable item is received in the office of delivery in a damaged condition, a notice shall be sent to the addressee requesting him to attend the post office within:

  • Seven days — in the case of domestic item
  • Fifteen days — in the case of international item

Regulation 55 — Redirection of Items

The sender of an item may avail the following facility in respect of the accountable domestic item and international inward item, by paying a postal fee of Rs. 6/-, without reference to the consent of the addressee:

  • (a) Recall of the item from the post (Provided that the item may be cancelled before it has been dispatched from the office of booking).
  • (b) Alteration in address or name of the addressee.

Reg. 55(2): The addressee of an item may avail the facility of alteration in address, free of charge if the original address and the substitute address are within the delivery area of the same post office.

Regulation 62 — Refusal of Items

  • The addressee of an item shall not be bound to pay the amount due on it if he does not want to take delivery; the word "Refused" shall be written by the Postman across the cover.
  • Unclaimed and refused items shall be returned, at once, direct to the offices of posting for delivery to the sender.

Regulation 64 — Detention at Post Office of Addressee

An item shall ordinarily be kept in deposit in the post office to which it is addressed for a period of seven days after all enquiries to find the addressee have proved unsuccessful.

Regulation 66 — Standard Remarks on Undelivered Items

Sl. Standard Remark Scenario Final Disposal
1RefusedAddressee is present but declines to acceptReturned to sender
2Addressee not foundAddress is located, but addressee not available (addressee specific delivery)Keep in deposit for 7 days; if nobody claims, returned to sender
3Addressee left without instructionsAddressee is known to have left without leaving forwarding instructionsReturned to sender
4Premises LockedMultiple attempts made but premises consistently found closedReturned to sender
5Insufficient AddressAddress is incomplete or inadequate to locate the recipientReturned to sender
6UnclaimedDelivery attempt made and notice served, but item not collected within prescribed timeReturned to sender
7DeceasedAddressee has passed awayReturn to sender
8RedirectedItem forwarded to a new address based on addressee's written instructionsRedirected on the same day
13Poste RestantePoste Restante (C/o Postmaster) item will be kept with the Postmaster for 15 days and if not claimed, returned to senderReturned to sender (after 15 days)

Regulation 67 — Detention at Returned Letter Office (RLO)

Items that remain undelivered to the addressee as well as the sender shall be detained at the Returned Letter Office for a period of —

  • (a) Fifteen days when they are unaccountable; and
  • (b) Thirty days when they are accountable.

RLO = An office that deals with unclaimed and refused items, or items without addresses, or with undecipherable or incomplete addresses.

Regulation 71 — Rates Chargeable on Unpaid Domestic Items

ConditionCharge
On an unpaid itemDouble the prepaid rate
On an insufficiently paid itemDouble the deficiency

Note: The postage or air mail fee actually charged shall in no case be less than Rupee One.
guru_explanation:
🧠 Guru's Take — Three Critical Numbers

  • 2 attempts = Maximum delivery attempts for accountable items (Reg. 42)
  • 7 days = Deposit at delivery post office + "Addressee not found" hold period (Reg. 64)
  • 15/30 days = RLO detention (unaccountable/accountable respectively) (Reg. 67)

💡 Redirection Fee — Rs. 6/- Rule

The fee for recall/redirection is Rs. 6/-. But addressee can redirect within same post office area free of charge. Always remember: once the item is out for delivery, no request can be entertained (Reg. 56).

🚫 Prohibited Items — Special Exceptions

  • Lottery materials — allowed if organised by Central or State Government.
  • Live animals — generally prohibited, but permitted in specific international cases (Reg. 27): bees, leeches, silk-worms, parasites for noxious insect control, Drosophilidae flies for biomedical research.
  • Currency notes — must be transmitted as insured items.
  • Batteries — prohibited by air; must go by surface only.

⚡ Exam Traps

  • After 2 failed delivery attempts, the item is never sent out again — only a notice is issued.
  • Damaged item notice: 7 days (domestic) vs 15 days (international) — easy to swap in MCQs.
  • RLO is not the delivery post office — it is a separate office handling undeliverable mail.
  • Poste Restante = kept with Postmaster for 15 days (same as unaccountable RLO detention — coincidence!).
  • Unpaid item charge = double the prepaid rate; insufficient = double the deficiency. Minimum charge = Re. 1/-.

title: Compensation for Loss & Damage — The Complete Chart
official_text:
💰 CHAPTER IV — COMPENSATION (Regulations 73–86)

The Post Office shall be liable to pay compensation for loss of item, abstraction of content, loss of content, damage to content, or damage to item, subject to conditions in this Chapter.

Regulation 73 — General Principles

  • Reg. 73(2): The compensation shall be payable to the sender. Provided that the compensation shall be payable to the addressee if the sender waives his right in favour of the addressee.
  • Reg. 73(3): The compensation for consequential loss or damage or any other such loss or damage shall NOT be payable.

Compensation Chart — All Categories at a Glance

Reg. Type of Item Compensation Amount
74 Domestic Registered Item Subject to a maximum of Rs. 100/- (Rupees One Hundred) or the actual value of contents, whichever is less.
74 International Registered Item 30 SDR
75 Domestic Speed Post For loss / damage / abstraction of content: Double the Speed Post charges OR Rs. 1,000/- (Rupees One Thousand), whichever is less.
For delay in delivery: Speed Post charges.
75 International Speed Post (EMS) For loss / damage / abstraction of content: 30 SDR.
For delay in delivery: Difference between the EMS charges and the registered post charges.
76 Domestic Insured Item The insured value or the actual value of the contents, whichever is less.
76 International Insured Item Subject to a maximum of the insured value or the actual value of contents, whichever is less. Compensation shall not exceed the insured amount.
77 India Post Parcel Subject to a maximum of Rs. 500/- (Rupees Five Hundred) or the actual value of contents, whichever is less.
78 International Air Parcel 40 SDR per parcel plus 4.50 SDR per kg
79 International Tracked Packet The compensation is restricted to ₹1,000/- or the actual declared value of the contents, whichever is less.
80 Domestic Money Order — Loss The amount of money order plus the commission paid.
80 Domestic Money Order — Delay The interest at the rate of savings bank account for the period of delay on the amount of money order.
80 International Money Remittance The amount of money remittance plus the commission paid.
81 VPP / COD — Loss of item Subject to a maximum of Rs. 500/- or actual value of contents, whichever is less.
81 VPP / COD — Amount collected but not remitted The amount collected.
Note: No liability if item is delivered to addressee and amount remitted to sender.

Regulation 82 — When NO Compensation Shall Be Payable

No compensation shall be payable —

  • (a) If the claim is not made within the period specified in Regulation 83;
  • (b) If the loss or damage is caused by the fault or negligence of the sender or the addressee;
  • (c) If the item contained anything prohibited from transmission by post;
  • (d) If the item was seized or detained by any competent authority under any law;
  • (e) If the sender has not packed the item securely;
  • (f) In case of "force majeure" events (e.g., natural disasters, war, civil commotion).

Reg. 82(2): The decision of the Department of Posts regarding the payment of compensation shall be final.

Regulation 83 — Time Limit for Claiming Compensation

The claim for compensation shall be preferred within the following time limits from the date of booking of the item:

  • (a) For domestic items: Three months.
  • (b) For international items: Six months (or as per UPU regulations).

Regulation 84 — Procedure for Claiming Compensation

  • The claim shall be submitted to the office of booking or the office of delivery.
  • The claimant shall produce the original receipt of booking along with the claim application.
  • The Department may require the claimant to produce evidence of the value of the contents.

Regulation 85 & 86 — Liability & Ex Gratia

  • Reg. 85: Liability of the Post Office shall be limited to the compensation amounts specified in this Chapter and shall not extend to any indirect or consequential loss or damage.
  • Reg. 86: The Department of Posts may, in exceptional cases, consider ex gratia payment, subject to the approval of the Director General, Postal Services.
guru_explanation:
🧠 Guru's Memory Map — The Magic Numbers

  • Domestic Registered = Rs. 100
  • Speed Post = Double charges OR Rs. 1,000 (whichever less)
  • India Post Parcel = Rs. 500
  • VPP/COD loss = Rs. 500
  • International Air Parcel = 40 SDR + 4.50 SDR/kg
  • International items (registered/EMS/tracked) = 30 SDR each

🎯 SDR = Special Drawing Rights

SDR is an international monetary unit used by UPU (Universal Postal Union) for international compensation. The actual rupee equivalent changes daily based on exchange rates. In exam questions, just remember the SDR numbers — don't worry about conversion.

⏰ Claim Time Limits

Think of it as: Domestic = 3 months; International = 6 months (double of domestic). Always measured from the date of booking, NOT from the date of loss or damage.

⚡ Top Exam Traps in Chapter IV

  • Compensation is payable to the sender (not the addressee) — unless the sender waives his right.
  • Consequential / indirect losses are NEVER compensated — only direct loss/damage.
  • If item contained prohibited goods, no compensation even if lost.
  • If sender packed poorly, no compensation — secure packing is the sender's duty.
  • Department's decision on compensation is final (Reg. 82(2)).
  • Ex gratia = needs approval of Director General, Postal Services — not the Postmaster.
practical_example:
📦 Compensation Scenarios — Practice Problems

Q1. A registered letter worth Rs. 250 is lost. What compensation is payable?
→ Max Rs. 100 or actual value (Rs. 250) — whichever is less → Rs. 100 (Reg. 74).

Q2. A Speed Post parcel worth Rs. 5,000 is lost. Speed Post charges paid = Rs. 80. What compensation?
→ Double the charges = Rs. 160; OR Rs. 1,000 — whichever is less → Rs. 160 (Reg. 75).

Q3. An India Post Parcel worth Rs. 2,000 is damaged. What is the compensation?
→ Max Rs. 500 or actual value — whichever is less → Rs. 500 (Reg. 77).

Q4. A Money Order of Rs. 1,000 is lost. Commission paid = Rs. 25. What is the compensation?
→ Amount of MO + commission = Rs. 1,025 (Reg. 80).

Q5. A Speed Post was delayed by 2 days. Charges paid = Rs. 50. What is the compensation?
→ For delay = Speed Post charges = Rs. 50 (Reg. 75).

Q6. A sender posted prohibited narcotics in a Speed Post. The item is lost. Is compensation payable?
→ No — item contained prohibited goods (Reg. 82(c)).

title: CCS (Joining Time) Rules, 1979 — Complete Guide: Scope, Admissibility, Amount & Pay
official_text:
CCS Rules
Rules 1–7 Complete

CCS (Joining Time) Rules, 1979

Notified vide GSR 695 dated 8th May, 1979 | Amended vide GSR 197 dated 10th March, 1989 and GSR 229(E) dated 27th March, 2015

LDCE IP PS Group B PM Grade I

📋 Rule 1 — Application & Scope

Joining Time is granted to a Government Servant when transferred to the control of another Government or organisation, in public interest.

These rules apply to all Government servants appointed in Civil Services and posts under the Central Government including work charged staff.

⛔ NOT Applicable To:

  • (a) Railway employees
  • (b) Armed Forces Personnel and those paid from defence services estimates
  • (c) Government servants engaged on contract and those not in whole-time employment
  • (d) Government servants paid out of contingencies

🔄 Rule 2 — Transfer & Deputation

When a Government servant is transferred to another Government/organisation which has made separate rules prescribing joining time, his joining time (for journey to join the new post and for return journey) shall be governed by those rules.

Exception: Unless different provisions are expressly made in the terms of deputation/foreign service by mutual agreement between the lending and borrowing authorities.

✅ Rule 4 — Admissibility of Joining Time

  • Granted on transfer in public interest to enable the servant to join the new post
  • No joining time for temporary transfer ≤ 180 days — only actual transit time allowed
  • Surplus staff transferred under Scheme Regulating Redeployment of Surplus Staff → eligible
  • Govt servants discharged due to reduction of establishment and reappointed to another Central Govt Office → entitled (subject to conditions)
  • Competitive exam/interview appointees (Central/State Govt employees) → eligible if they opt for counting past service

🚫 Transfer on Own Request:

Joining Time is NOT admissible. The intervening period may be regularized by grant of leave applicable to him. [OM No. 19011/33/81-Allowances dt. 29.01.1983]

📅 Rule 5 — Commencement & Amount of Joining Time

Charge given in FORENOON
SAME DATE
Joining time starts from that very day
Charge given in AFTERNOON
NEXT DATE
Joining time starts from following day

Same Station Transfer (No Change of Residence):

Maximum: 1 day only

Inter-Station Transfer (Change of Residence) — Distance-Based Table:

Distance Between Old HQ & New HQ Normal Joining Time If Road Travel >200 km Necessarily Continuous
Up to 1,000 km 10 days 12 days
More than 1,000 km 12 days 15 days
More than 2,000 km 15 days
(12 days if travel by air)		 15 days

🏝️ Special Remote Area Provision:

Transfer to/from North Eastern Region, Sikkim, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Ladakh → +2 additional days over and above the normal joining time. [Rule 5 & Notification dt. 27.03.2015]

Distance = Actual distance travelled, not weighted mileage for which fare is charged by Railways in ghat/hill regions.

💳 Rule 6 — Crediting & Combination of Joining Time

  • Unutilized joining time → credited to Earned Leave account [CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972 — Rule 26]
  • Joining time may be combined with vacation and/or regular leave of any kind or duration EXCEPT Casual Leave

🔀 Revised Transfer Orders While In Transit:

If directed to a different place while in transit → joining time already availed = counted as fresh spell. Full joining time afresh from the date following receipt of revised orders. [Rule 6 & Notification dt. 27.03.2015]

💰 Rule 7 — Joining Time Pay & Allowances

A Government servant on joining time is treated as ON DUTY during the entire period.

✅
ENTITLED TO
  • Joining Time Pay (= last pay drawn)
  • Dearness Allowance (DA)
  • House Rent Allowance (of old station)
⛔
NOT ENTITLED TO
  • Conveyance Allowance
  • Permanent Travelling Allowance
  • City Compensatory Allowance (abolished — 6th CPC)

Joining time pay shall be paid by the new administrative authority where such Govt servant joins on transfer. [Rule 7 & Notification dt. 27.03.2015]

practical_example:
Case Studies

Real Scenarios — Apply the Rules

CASE 1

Ramesh, a PA in Mumbai GPO, is transferred in public interest to Kolkata. Distance: 1,900 km. He hands over charge at 11:00 AM on 10th April 2026.

Calculation:

  • Distance 1,900 km → More than 1,000 km → 12 days normal joining time
  • Charge given in forenoon (11:00 AM) → Joining time starts 10th April itself
  • He must join by 21st April 2026 (10th + 11 more days = 21st)
  • If he joins on 18th April → Unused 3 days → Credited to Earned Leave
CASE 2

Sunita is transferred from Delhi to Port Blair (Andaman & Nicobar Islands). Distance: 2,400 km. She must travel by road for 220 km.

Calculation:

  • Distance 2,400 km → More than 2,000 km
  • Road travel >200 km → 15 days (not the air-reduced 12 days)
  • Port Blair = Andaman & Nicobar → +2 days remote area bonus
  • Total Joining Time = 15 + 2 = 17 days
CASE 3

Vijay requests a transfer from Hyderabad to Chennai (own request). Distance: 700 km. He asks: Can I get joining time?

Answer:

No joining time is admissible on transfer on own request. The intervening period between relinquishment at Chennai and taking charge at Hyderabad can only be regularized as leave (EL/HPL etc.) applicable to him. [OM No. 19011/33/81-Allowances dt. 29.01.1983]

CASE 4

Priya is transferred from Delhi to Pune (1,400 km) and while in transit, gets revised orders directing her to Bengaluru instead. She had availed 5 days of joining time so far.

Rule 6 — Fresh Spell Principle:

  • 5 days already availed = treated as fresh spell (not wasted)
  • From the day after she receives revised orders → full fresh joining time starts again
  • Delhi → Bengaluru = ~2,150 km → More than 2,000 km → 15 days fresh

❓ Who pays Joining Time Pay?

New administrative authority (not the old one). Common trick — don't confuse with old station.

Only when the entire journey is by air. The maximum is capped at 12 days in that case (not 15).

title: Book of Branch Office Rules — Mail Handling, Registration & Accounts
official_text:
📬 BOOK OF BRANCH OFFICE RULES

Mail Handling · Registration & Insurance · Accounts & Remittances — Complete Operational Guide

🔐 1. Tampered Bags & Letter Box Clearance (Rules 53, 59)

Rule 53 — Bags Received with Signs of Tampering: If a bag is found with missing cash/articles or signs of tampering:

  1. Report immediately to the Superintendent and the dispatching office/section.
  2. Preserve the bag and label (without detaching the seal/cord). Mark them with initials and the date stamp.
  3. Record the irregularity in the Error Book.

Rule 59 — Clearance of Letter-Boxes:

Aspect Rule
Clearance TimeAt hours fixed by the ASPOs/SDI.
Paid ArticlesArticles intended for delivery from the branch office itself should be delivered immediately.
SortingAll other articles are sorted according to the sorting list or set aside for dispatch to the Account Office.
Stamping RuleUnregistered articles received in sorting for dispatch must NOT be stamped by the Branch Office.
Invalid StampsNon-Indian postage stamps cannot be accepted and should not be defaced.

📦 2. Unpaid Articles, Check Slips & Labelled Bundles (Rules 62, 64, 65)

Rule 62 — Unpaid and Insecure Articles:

  • Action: Open or insecure inland articles found in the letter-box or sorting must be securely closed.
  • Taxing: Stamp with "Postage Due" if unpaid/insufficiently paid. Note the amount due before forwarding.
  • Accounting: Do NOT credit the unpaid postage amount in the BO Account or Journal (PA-5).
  • Foreign Post: An article received by foreign post must never be taxed with postage by the branch office.

Rule 64 — Check Slips (MS-10): A check slip is a label tied to the top of labeled bundles.

Colour Used For
🩷 PinkOrdinary Station Paid and Unpaid Bundle
⬜ WhiteOrdinary Sorting Bundle (used for both Express and Deferred). Note: Two diagonal blue lines indicate an Express bundle.
🟦 Blue (with "Air Mail")Foreign air mail bundles

Rule 65 — Labelled Bundles:

Bundle Type Definition & Threshold
Station BundleContains unregistered articles for a particular station. Prepared when articles number 15 or more.
Sorting BundleContains unregistered articles for many stations.
Territorial BundleA sorting bundle prepared for a specific state or tract of country. Prepared when articles number 25 or more.
Express BundleRequires immediate sorting upon receipt.
Deferred BundleCan be disposed of later.

📮 3. Delivery & Postage Taxing (Rules 66, 67)

Rule 66 — Delivery of Unregistered Articles:

  • Stamping: Unregistered articles received for delivery must be date-stamped on the back (except postcards, which are stamped on the address side).
  • Redirection: If given to a village postman/agent for delivery outside the town/village, they must be stamped again.
  • Postage Due: Amounts due on unpaid articles must be entered in the BO Journal (PA-5).
  • Foreign Post: An article received by foreign post must never be taxed with postage by the branch office.

Rule 67 — Postage Taxing at Branch Office:

  • BPM must properly tax all unpaid/insufficiently paid unregistered articles posted at the BO and intended for local delivery.
  • Registered Newspapers: The office of posting is responsible for correct postage. The office of delivery should generally not challenge this unless negligence is suspected, in which case a report is made to the Superintendent.

📜 4. Registration, Insurance & Acknowledgement (Rules 77, 79, 80, 85, 93, 94)

Rule / Form Key Points
Registered Journal
RP-51 | Rule 77		 Records receipts given to senders of ordinary registered articles (excluding V.P. and insured). Contains 200 receipts with printed serial numbers running from 1 to 200.
Registered & Parcel Lists
Rule 79		 Registered List: Form RP-32. Parcel List: Form RP-3. Corrections to entry numbers or office of posting must be initialed by BPM. No correction is allowed in the total — if total is incorrect, the list must be destroyed and a fresh one prepared.
Acknowledgement
Rule 80		 Registered articles addressed to a foreign country requiring an acknowledgement must be clearly marked with "Avis de reception".
Registered Articles in Letter Box
Rule 85		 If an inland article marked "Registered" is found in the letter box, it must be registered immediately. If not fully prepaid, charge a fee equal to double the usual registration fee plus the postage due.
Conditions of Insurance
Rule 93		 Registered letters and parcels (including V.P.) may be insured at a Branch Office up to the value of Rs. 600 for authorized offices.
Insured Articles
Rule 94		 Consult Post Office Guide Volume III to verify if destination office accepts insured articles (ensure no symbol "B" or "L" indicates restriction). Acknowledgements for inland insured letters (RP-54) are free. Foreign insured letters require a special fee if acknowledgement is requested.

💰 5. Accounts, Remittances & BO Daily Account (Rules 124, 129, 130, 134)

Rule / Form Key Points
Branch Office Account
PA-6 | Rule 124		 Records monetary transactions between BO and Account Office.
Exclusion: Cash realized from postage collections must never be included in "Cash collected".
V.P. Articles: Amounts collected for V.P. articles delivered are credited under "Money orders issued".
Reply Coupons: Value of stamps exchanged for reply-coupons is shown under "Unclassified payments".
Monthly Abstract in B.O. Bag
PA-7 | Rule 129		 The B.O. bag closed on the 1st of each month must contain the Abstract of Monetary Transactions for the entire preceding month. This abstract is submitted in Form PA-7.
Remittances Sent Through Post
Rule 130		 Cloth Bags: Used for remittances of currency notes only, up to Rs. 500.
Leather Cash Bags: Used for remittances including coins or exceeding Rs. 500.
BO Daily Account
ACG-22(a) | Rule 134		 Entries from BO Account are copied into BO Daily Account (ACG-22(a)).
Nil Transactions: On days with no monetary transaction, submit the account in form ACG-22(c) instead of ACG-22(a).
Account Office Documents (Chapter 9):
• B.O. Slip (PA-4): Primary communication and accounting slip sent from Account Office to Branch Office.
• B.O. Summary (ACG-3(a)): Summary document prepared at Account Office to consolidate and record daily transactions of the Branch Office.

🧠 Guru's Master Framework — "TUBE-RAIDS"

Remember Part 2 of BO Rules in 10 blocks: Tampering → Unpaid articles → Bundles → Express/Deferred → Registration → Acknowledgement → Insurance → Daily Accounts → Sorting. Each block has signature numbers/rules that examiners frequently test.

Foreign post taxingNEVER taxed with postage by BORule 66

Acknowledgement marking (foreign)"Avis de reception"Rule 80

Insurance limit at BORs. 600 (for authorized offices)Rule 93
Inland insured letter acknowledgementRP-54 | FREE for inlandRule 94
V.P. amounts collectedCredited under "Money orders issued" in PA-6Rule 124

Nil transaction day formACG-22(c) instead of ACG-22(a)Rule 134

⚡ Common Exam Traps — BO Rules (Mail Handling & Accounts)

  • Station Bundle requires ≥ 15 articles; Territorial Bundle requires ≥ 25 articles — don't mix these up.
  • White check slip is used for BOTH Express and Deferred bundles. The distinction: two diagonal blue lines = Express.
  • Unregistered articles for dispatch must NOT be stamped by the Branch Office (Rule 59) — only articles for local delivery are date-stamped.
  • Postcard stamping is on the address side; all other unregistered articles are stamped on the back.
  • "Registered" article found in letter box — the penalty is DOUBLE the registration fee, not just the ordinary fee.
  • Cloth bag = only currency notes, up to Rs. 500. As soon as there are coins or the amount exceeds Rs. 500 → use Leather Cash Bag.
  • V.P. collections go under "Money orders issued" in PA-6 — NOT under "Cash collected". Postage collections also never go under "Cash collected".
  • On a day with no monetary transactions, submit ACG-22(c) (Nil form), not ACG-22(a).
  • Corrections to totals in Registered/Parcel Lists are strictly prohibited — destroy and prepare a fresh list.
practical_example:
📦 Practice Scenarios — BO Rules (Mail Handling & Accounts)

Q1. A Branch Office receives a bag with the cord broken and some articles missing. What are the three steps the BPM must take?
→ (1) Report immediately to the Superintendent and dispatching office. (2) Preserve the bag and label without detaching seal/cord, mark with initials and date stamp. (3) Record the irregularity in the Error Book (Rule 53).

Q2. During sorting, the BPM finds 30 unregistered articles destined for Delhi. Should a Station Bundle or Territorial Bundle be prepared?
→ Since there are 30 articles (≥15) for a particular station (Delhi), prepare a Station Bundle. A Territorial Bundle would require ≥ 25 articles for a specific state/territory (Rule 65).

Q3. A postcard is received at the Branch Office for delivery. On which side must the date stamp be applied?
→ On the address side (postcards are the exception; all other unregistered articles are stamped on the back) (Rule 66).

Q4. An inland article marked "Registered" is found in the letter box. It has insufficient postage. What action must the BPM take and what penalty applies?
→ The BPM must register it immediately. Penalty: charge equal to double the usual registration fee plus the postage due (Rule 85).

Q5. A Branch Office remits Rs. 350/- in currency notes only to the Account Office. What type of bag should be used?
→ A Cloth Bag — it contains only currency notes and the amount is within Rs. 500 (Rule 130).

Q6. On a particular Sunday, there are no monetary transactions at the BO. What form must be submitted to the Account Office?
→ ACG-22(c) (BO Daily Account — Nil) must be submitted instead of ACG-22(a) (Rule 134).

Q7. The BPM realizes the total of a Registered List (RP-32) is incorrect. What should he do?
→ He must destroy the list and prepare a fresh one. No correction is allowed in the total of entries (Rule 79).

Q8. A customer wants an acknowledgement for an inland insured letter. What form is used and what is the fee?
→ Form RP-54. The acknowledgement for inland insured letters is FREE (Rule 94).

title: GDS Penalties, Disciplinary Procedure & Conduct Rules
official_text:
GDS DISCIPLINARY FRAMEWORK — PENALTIES, PROCEDURE & CONDUCT

Rules 9 to 14, 21 & 22 — Complete disciplinary ecosystem for Gramin Dak Sevaks

Rule 9 — Nature of Penalties

⚡ Minor Penalties (1–5)

  1. Censure
  2. Debarring from MTS/Postman/Mail Guard/PA/SA recruitment — up to 3 years
  3. Debarring from MTS recruitment (selection-cum-seniority) — up to 3 years
  4. Recovery from TRCA of pecuniary loss caused by negligence/breach
  5. Withholding of annual TRCA increment — without cumulative effect — up to 3 years

🔴 Major Penalties (6–9)

  1. Reduction to lower TRCA stage for period exceeding 3 years (not permanent)
  2. Compulsory Discharge — with monetary benefits (SDBS + Gratuity proportionate)
  3. Removal from engagement — NOT a disqualification for future engagement
  4. Dismissal — SHALL ordinarily be a disqualification for future engagement

Rules 10-A to 10-G — Disciplinary Procedure

Rule 10-A: Procedure for Minor Penalty

No order for Minor Penalty (Rules 1–5) shall be passed EXCEPT after:
(a) Sevak is informed in writing of the proposal and allegations and given opportunity to represent.
(b) Representation, if any, is considered by the Engaging Authority.

Rule 10-B: Procedure for Major Penalty

No order for Major Penalty (Rules 6–9) shall be passed EXCEPT after:
(a) Sevak is informed in writing and given opportunity to represent.
(b) Representation is considered by the Engaging Authority.

Rule 10-D: Mandatory Inquiry (Major Penalty)

Inquiry is mandatory for major penalties even if GDS accepts charges. Purpose: to give GDS adequate opportunity to defend. Exception: If charge is accepted unconditionally, no inquiry needed.

Rule 10-E: Discretionary Inquiry (Minor Penalty)

For minor penalties, inquiry is NOT mandatory — it is at the discretion of the Disciplinary/Engaging Authority. However, if GDS requests inspection of documents or cross-examination, authority must apply its mind carefully.

Rule 10-F: Procedure After Discharge (at age 65)

If departmental proceedings were instituted while the Sevak was in engagement and the Sevak subsequently gets discharged at age 65, the proceedings shall continue as if the Sevak had continued in engagement. The authority's function is to reach a finding and submit report to the President. No appeal shall lie against such decision.

Rule 10-G: Proceedings After Discharge (not instituted during engagement)

If proceedings were NOT instituted during engagement and GDS is discharged at 65 years, fresh proceedings:
(i) Require sanction of the President.
(ii) Cannot relate to events more than 4 years before institution.
(iii) Conducted as per procedure for dismissal from engagement.

Rule 11 — When Rule 10 Procedure Does NOT Apply

The disciplinary procedure under Rule 10 shall NOT be followed in 3 situations:

  1. Where penalty is imposed due to conviction on criminal charge
  2. Where the authority is satisfied that it is not reasonably practicable to hold inquiry (recorded in writing)
  3. Where the President is satisfied that it is not expedient in the interest of security of the State

Rule 12 — Put Off Duty

When can a Sevak be Put Off Duty?

  • When disciplinary proceedings are contemplated or pending
  • When a criminal case is under investigation / inquiry / trial

Special Authority — Fraud/Embezzlement Cases

Inspector of Post Offices or ASPO can put GDS off duty under immediate intimation to Engaging Authority. Such order is effective for 15 days only unless confirmed by Engaging Authority.

Ex-Gratia Compensation during Put Off Duty

Period of Put Off Duty Compensation
First 90 days25% of TRCA + admissible DA per month
Beyond 90 days (prolonged, not Sevak's fault)May be increased up to 50% of compensation for first 90 days
Beyond 90 days (prolonged due to Sevak's fault)May be reduced up to 50% of compensation for first 90 days
Absconding / Unauthorized AbsenceNO ex-gratia compensation

Special provision: If major penalty proceedings end with only a minor penalty — the Sevak gets full TRCA + allowances for the put off duty period.

Rules 13 & 14 — Appeal

Who can Appeal?

A Sevak may appeal against:
• An order putting him off duty
• Any penalty under Rule 9
Appeal goes to the authority immediately superior to the one who passed the order.

Time Limit for Appeal

3 months from the date of receiving copy of the order. Appellate Authority may entertain late appeal if sufficient cause is shown.

Rules 19 & 20 — Revision & Review

Rule 19 — Revision

Regional PMG / Head of Circle / superior authority may revise orders at any time. Revision cannot be done after 6 months from the order date (except by Govt./Head of Circle/PMG Region), and also not before expiry of 3 months appeal period.

Rule 20 — Review

The President may review any order passed under these rules when new material or evidence — not available at the time of the original order — comes to light, which changes the nature of the case.

GDS Conduct Rules — Rules 21 & 22

Rule 21 — General Conduct

Every Sevak shall at all times:
(i) Maintain absolute integrity
(ii) Maintain devotion to duty
(iii) Do nothing which is unbecoming of a Sevak

Rule 21-A — Promptness & Courtesy

No Sevak shall:
(i) Act in discourteous manner in official duties
(ii) Adopt dilatory tactics or wilfully cause delay in disposal of work

Rule 21-B — Sexual Harassment

No GDS shall indulge in sexual harassment of any woman at any workplace. Sevak in charge of workplace shall take steps to PREVENT sexual harassment.

Rule 22 — Politics & Elections

No Sevak shall be member of / associated with any political party or political activity. Duty to prevent family members from subversive political activities and report inability to do so to the Government.

guru_explanation:
🧠 Dak Guru Decodes — Why This Circular Matters

This circular is a landmark update. It officially notifies the 10 major product rationalization changes under the Post Office Regulations, 2024 (effective 16.12.2024). The key theme is: "One Product One Need" — multiple old products with overlapping features have been merged into single, clearly-named products. This is high-yield content for both LDCE IP and PS Group B exams.

📬 1. Postcard — Simplest Change to Remember

Five old postcard variants (PC, Reply PC, Printed PC, Competition PC, Meghdoot PC) are all merged into a single Postcard at ₹0.50. The confusion of different cards with different rates ends here. Remember: just ₹0.50 for any postcard.

✉️ 2. Letters — Weight Cap Cut to 500g

The weight limit for Letters has been drastically cut from 2 kg to 500 grams. Anything above 500g must now go as a parcel (India Post Parcel). This is a trap question: "What is the maximum weight of a letter under PO Regulations 2024?" Answer: 500 grams.

📚 3. Book Post — No More Minimum, Ads Allowed

All three old book packet categories are merged into one Book Post. Two new liberalizations: (1) no minimum number of items required, and (2) books with advertisements can also be sent — a change from the earlier restriction.

📦 4 & 5. India Post Parcel — Retail vs Contractual

The old Registered Parcel becomes India Post Parcel – Retail (for individuals). The old Business Parcel becomes India Post Parcel – Contractual (for bulk/business customers who sign agreements). Both have the same value-added services (COD, Insurance, Proof of Delivery), but contractual customers must execute a formal agreement. The volumetric weight concept is newly introduced — you will be charged on gross or volumetric weight, whichever is higher.

💵 6. Indian Postal Order — Only ₹10 and Above

All denominations below Rs. 10 have been scrapped. IPOs now come only in ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, and ₹100. Smaller denominations were simply not being used in practice.

📰 7 & 8. The Newspaper vs. Periodical Distinction — MOST IMPORTANT CHANGE

This is the core subject of the circular. The definitions now come from the Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023:

  • Registered Newspaper = Only publications in loose folded sheets, published at intervals of up to 7 days (daily or weekly). These get concessional newspaper tariff.
  • Periodical Post = Any publication published at regular intervals with a gap of more than 7 days is treated as a periodical and charged at periodical rates (not newspaper rates).
  • BOTH cannot be posted in letter boxes — they must be posted at the counter.

💳 9. COD (Retail) — ₹10,000 Limit

The old Value Payable Post (VPP) is renamed Cash on Delivery (COD) — Retail. The maximum booking amount has doubled from Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 10,000. Everything else about VPP is retained.

💸 10. Money Order — Limits & Zero Commission Cases

The old eMO merges into a single Money Order product. Key figures to remember: Single MO cap = ₹10,000; Monthly per-payee limit = ₹25,000. Commission rate stays the same. Important: Zero commission for PM Relief Fund, PM CARES Fund, and CM Relief Fund remittances.

⚡ Quick Recap — The 10 Changes in 30 Seconds

  1. Multiple postcards → One Postcard @ ₹0.50
  2. Letters weight: 2 kg → 500 gms
  3. Book packets merged → Book Post (no minimum, ads allowed)
  4. Registered Parcel → IP Parcel – Retail (volumetric weight + merchandise declaration)
  5. Business Parcel → IP Parcel – Contractual (agreement needed)
  6. IPO denominations below ₹10 gone → only ₹10, 20, 50, 100
  7. Newspaper = loosely folded, ≤ 7 days interval
  8. Periodical = > 7 days interval, Periodical Post rates
  9. VPP → COD Retail, limit raised to ₹10,000
  10. eMO → Money Order, cap ₹10,000 / month ₹25,000

📦 Scenario-Based Questions

Q1. A publisher releases a magazine every Sunday (weekly). Is it a Newspaper or a Periodical under PO Regulations 2024?
→ Registered Newspaper — published weekly (7-day interval), in loosely folded sheets. Eligible for concessional newspaper tariff.

Q2. A fortnightly magazine (published every 15 days) claims newspaper rates. Is it allowed?
→ No — gap is more than 7 days, so it is a Periodical and must be sent under Periodical Post at periodical rates.

Q3. A customer wants to send a letter weighing 700 grams. Can it be sent as a Letter?
→ No — Letters under PO Regulations 2024 are limited to 500 grams. It must be sent as an India Post Parcel.

Q4. A bulk book-seller wants to post sample books. Under old rules, he needed a minimum quantity. Is that still required?
→ No — under Book Post (PO Regulations 2024), no minimum number of items is required to be posted.

Q5. A customer sends a VPP (Value Payable) item worth Rs. 8,000 for COD collection. Is this permissible?
→ Yes — under the new Cash on Delivery (Retail), the max booking amount is Rs. 10,000. Rs. 8,000 is within limit.

Q6. A customer sends a donation of Rs. 5,000 through Money Order to the PM CARES Fund. How much commission is charged?
→ Nil (Zero commission) — remittances to PM CARES Fund / PM Relief Fund / CM Relief Fund are exempt from commission.

Q7. A company dispatches 50 parcels daily. What type of parcel service do they use?
→ India Post Parcel – Contractual — bulk/contractual customers must execute a formal agreement with the Department.

Q8. A parcel weighs 1 kg physically, but its dimensions give a volumetric weight of 1.5 kg. Which weight is used for tariff?
→ 1.5 kg (volumetric) — under India Post Parcel, the higher of gross or volumetric weight applies.
